subject: SDK bootstrap, auth & routing + queues for Dedicated capacity — alignment and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Subject: SDK bootstrap, auth & routing + queues for Dedicated capacity — alignment and next steps

Hi Eliot — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and action items so we have a clear path for your Dedicated deployment and the initial integration: 

Summary of agreed scope
- Dedicated capacity for customer-facing inference of FinFore Assist (text generation + embeddings/rerank).
- Initial traffic profile: pilot ~300 requests/min, typical prompt 120 tokens in + ~150 tokens out.
- Hard latency goal: p95 < 200ms for short text generation paths; fallback to hosted model variant for burst overflow.

Key technical items we discussed 
1) SDK bootstrap & auth
- Start with our Python SDK (pip install redwood-inference) for the pilot. We support both API-key and OIDC-based auth.
- For Private/Dedicated we recommend OIDC service accounts + customer-managed KMS for secret wrapping (better for auditability).
- mTLS is supported for Private deployments on-prem; for cloud VPC we typically use OIDC + mutual peering + flow logs.

2) Routing & model variants
- Routing policy: route production traffic to the pinned Dedicated model; overflow routes to a cost-optimized hosted variant.
- You can route by header (X-FinFore-Region), latency budget, or cost tier. We'll provide a sample routing policy config.

3) Structured output / tool-calling
- Redwood supports structured function-calling (JSON schema enforcement). We recommend adding a lightweight post-processor to validate outputs for the first 2 weeks of the pilot.

4) Embeddings & reranker
- Workflow: batch-embed existing corpus offline -> build ANN index (we recommend Faiss/ScaNN) -> serve reranker as a secondary pass on Dedicated.
- We'll provide an embeddings throughput plan; initial indexing can run on Hosted or Dedicated depending on data residency needs.

5) Dedicated capacity sizing & queues
- Baseline estimate: target 300 req/min -> peak burst to 600 req/min. Assuming 270 tokens average per request (in+out), estimate ~1.6M tokens/hour.
- Suggested concurrency and queue config: per-GPU concurrency 8 active streams, queue depth 100 requests, autoscale target 70% GPU utilization.
- Warm pool: 2 pre-warmed instances for sub-second cold-start behavior on ramp days.

Attachments and artifacts
- Attached: finfore-integration-checklist.xlsx and rd-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (high level).
- I'll upload the SOW draft after we finalize scope; Marissa will own contract pathing.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates)
- Ben: send a runnable SDK + routing sample (config + minimal server) by Thu, 2026-07-22. (Owner: Ben)
- Eliot/FinFore: confirm whether you prefer OIDC or API-key for the pilot and share security contact. (Owner: Eliot)
- Marissa: push SOW draft for initial legal review by Fri, 2026-07-24. (Owner: Marissa)

Would love confirmation on the auth preference and whether the traffic estimate matches your expectations. If yes, we'll schedule a 30-minute tech handoff to run the sample and validate perf assumptions.

Thanks,

— Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga — that recap is super helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Auth preference
- Security prefers OIDC with short-lived service tokens and automatic rotation. We can create a service account and the OIDC provider once we have the full redirect/metadata. mTLS is an option later but let's avoid it for the pilot.

2) Routing
- We want header-based routing (X-FinFore-Env: prod|staging) and a latency-based fallback. Can you share a minimal routing policy that supports both?

3) Concurrency assumptions
- Your tokens/hour calc looks reasonable. For the pilot we expect some heavier embeddings runs (~batching 512) which may run on separate Dedicated nodes off-peak.

4) Timeline
- We want to run the pilot the week of Aug 10–14. Is that realistic if Ben can get the sample by Thu?

Security contact: Lina Park (lina.park@finfore.io) — she'll coordinate OIDC metadata.

Appreciate the attach — will review and revert.

Eliot — quick technical notes and a minimal sample you can use to validate locally.

1) Sample SDK usage (Python)
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(auth_method="oidc", oidc_token_path="/tmp/finfore_token.json")
resp = client.generate(model="finfore-dedicated-v1", prompt="Summarize the following...", max_tokens=150)
print(resp.text)
```

2) Minimal routing policy (YAML)
- route by header X-FinFore-Env, fall back by latency budget:
```
routing:
  - match: header(X-FinFore-Env)=="prod"
    destination: finfore-dedicated-v1
  - match: latency > 250ms
    destination: finfore-hosted-cost-variant
```

3) Throughput math and queue config rationale
- Measured on our quantized 70B variant: ~3200 tokens/sec per V100-equivalent GPU when serving batched requests.
- For your expected 270 tokens/request -> ~12 requests/sec per GPU at full utilization (~720 requests/min).
- We recommend starting with 2 GPUs (headroom for 1.5x bursts) with per-GPU concurrency 8 and queue depth 100. Autoscaler target: 65–75% GPU utilization.
- Embeddings: batched 512 gives best throughput; run those jobs on separate nodes or schedule in off-peak windows.

4) Cold-start / KV cache warmup
- If you use KV cache optimizations (long-context), include a 90–120s warmup window when scaling up so the cache doesn't thrash. Warm pool of 2 instances mitigates this.

I'll commit a runnable repo with the SDK sample + routing config and a small load script by Thu morning. That will let you run a simple local perf check and validate the numbers before the pilot.

If you want, we can pre-provision the 2 GPU nodes in a sandbox tenant for you to run SSH load tests.

— Ben
